title: The text is indexed by W through a newtype instead of to_usize at each load
body:
`merge` and `find_lcp` in `libsufr/src/build/sort.rs` and `compare` in `libsufr/src/search.rs` index the text with values loaded from a `W` array, so each index is `text[(y[idx_y] + full_len_lcp).to_usize()]` or `text[suffix_pos + full_offset]` after a `to_usize` on the load. The `Int` trait in `libsufr/src/io.rs` provides `to_usize` and `from_usize`, since `as` cannot be written on a type parameter.

## Proposal

A newtype over the text, `struct Text<'a>(&'a [u8])`, with `impl<W: Int> Index<W>` and `Index<Range<W>>`, so `text[suffix]` takes a `W` and the cast sits once in the `Index` impl. About six `to_usize` calls in the hot loops go. Stores into `W` arrays are unchanged, so `from_usize` stays.

## Cost

A wrapper type between the reader and a slice, which `concrete-first` counts against. The `Index` impl is inlined, and the benchmark says whether that holds: `merge` and `find_lcp` are hot loops, so the build before and after goes on one board, 4 threads, 5 repeats, medians, and `count` over the 10 MiB build in each memory mode beside it.

## Open

Two things decide it, and both are judged on the diff: whether the code reads as simpler with the casts out of the loops, and whether any row of the benchmark moves. A loss on either is a no. It follows `sufr-cad4f6` and the change that types `merge`'s locals as `usize`, since that change removes most of the other casts first.
close_reason: Worked through as a proof of concept on the current code: with the text as Memory<u8>, the one line that gains is the byte compare in merge, which loses two to_usize calls. The call to find_lcp and every other cast in the loops are on lengths and positions used in arithmetic, which Index cannot take. Against that stand a Deref, two Index impls and &Memory<u8> on seven signatures. Jack judged it not worth it on 2026-11-04. The casts in those loops are instead reduced by typing merge's locals as usize, which is its own change after sufr-cad4f6.
